newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's agro-exports to earn $15 bln in '97-paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's agro-exports to earn $15 bln in '97-paper.

text.p: Revenue from Brazilian exports of agricultural products should hit $15 billion in 1997, an increase of almost 20 percent on 1996, financial daily Gazeta Mercantil said.
The jump will translate into a positive balance of more than $8 billion for trade in agricultural products, the paper quoted Agriculture Minister Arlindo Porto as saying.
The rise was due to a combination of larger harvests and high prices for commodities on international markets, it added.
In the first five months of the year, coffee, soybean and soy product exports were largely responsible for the accumulated 4.6 percent increase in Brazil's external sales, Gazeta said.
In May, Brazil posted a $271 million trade deficit, the lowest in 12 months thanks to the contribution of agricultural exports.
